blocks.x: Engineering standards & stack

items: W3C Verifiable Credentials
Credentials that verify cryptographically without phoning home to a vendor.
permissioned DLT
Shared ledgers with known counterparties and governed writes — DLT where it earns its keep.
notarized audit exports
Evidence exports sealed so nobody can quietly edit last quarter's numbers.
hash-linked anchoring
Records anchored by hash so tampering is detectable — trust with a checksum.

items: traceability ledgers
Lot-level history from source to shelf, verifiable by the parties who need to verify it.
food-safety labs
Safety results joined to lots and suppliers — traceability that works the day you need it.
processing line historians
Line data streamed with the tags that matter, ready for the twin and the OEE math.
cold-chain telemetry
Temperature integrity tracked from dock to shelf, with excursions raised as events, not discovered as losses.

blocks.x: Operational telemetry
The measures that decide gate outcomes, generated in-flight:

items: audit evidence prep
Evidence gathered continuously during the period, so the audit opens prepared instead of panicked.
dispute resolution time
Dispute cycle time measured from raise to resolution, with the stage that stalled it identified.
reconciliation breaks
Breaks counted at source per cycle, with aging reported — none carried past the quarter unexplained.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship
The ways programs like this die — and the guard we ship against each:

items: On-chain PII
On-chain PII: personal data never touches the ledger; only salted hashes and pointers are anchored; the guard is part of the first slice, not a hardening phase
Key fragility
Key fragility — guarded because root keys live in HSMs under dual control with ceremony logs; rotation is rehearsed, not documented
Ledger worship
Ledger worship — a chain only helps where counterparties dispute truth; workflows that already trust one database stay on one database
